innovators.name: Denis UWIHIRWE
innovators.bio:
Denis Uwihirwe is a Senior Software Engineer, System Administrator, and Managing Director of Email DenSend LTD, based in Kigali, Rwanda. Holding a Bachelor’s degree in Computer and Software Engineering from the University of Rwanda's College of Science and Technology, he possesses extensive experience designing scalable distributed systems, real-time data architectures, and mission-critical cloud infrastructure. He seamlessly bridges complex backend engineering with production-grade systems administration to build highly available, fault-tolerant platforms.

Denis specializes in architecting high-performance backend systems and data pipelines using Spring Boot, Node.js, Express.js, Next.js, TypeScript, Python, and C++. His technical mastery extends to event-driven architectures and real-time streaming pipelines—leveraging PostgreSQL, ClickHouse, Apache Pulsar, Debezium, Redis, and MinIO—alongside containerization, automated CI/CD workflows, reverse proxy routing, and Linux server administration. Driven by a commitment to engineering excellence, he leads developer platform initiatives, delivers technical infrastructure training, and integrates modern AI-assisted engineering practices to deliver robust, enterprise-grade software solutions.

innovators.name: Aime Serge UKOBIZABA
innovators.bio:
Most startups struggle to build inclusive, secure, available ,and scalable systems that can grow with their users and perform reliably in real-world environments.



I am a Software Engineer focused on building secure and scalable cloud applications, with expertise in backend systems, API development, and full-stack engineering. I design solutions that are not only functional but also resilient, maintainable, and ready for long-term growth. Currently, I'm developing INEZA AI Venture under ALU CHII.



My work centers on: 

• Backend & API systems for scalable applications 

• Cloud-powered architectures for performance and reliability 

• AI-powered solutions, including AI agents and intelligent systems 

• Mobile and full-stack application development 

• Cybersecurity-aware engineering and secure system design With training from ALX and exposure to modern technologies including cloud platforms and AI systems. 



I bring a systems-thinking approach to solving complex problems and building impactful digital solutions. I combine software engineering, cloud architecture, and cybersecurity principles to deliver applications that meet both technical and business needs.If you're building a product or startup and need a Software Engineer to develop secure, scalable backend systems, APIs, AI-powered solutions, or full-stack applications, I’d be glad to connect.

projects.description: HitamoSpace is a digital platform developed under UR Binary Hub to manage venue booking, event registration, QR-code attendance, and graduation ceremony operations through a centralized and intelligent event management system.
projects.full_description: HitamoSpace is a flagship homegrown digital solution developed under UR Binary Hub at the University of Rwanda to modernize venue and event management. The platform enables institutions to manage venue reservations, event registration, participant verification, attendance tracking, and real-time analytics through a centralized digital ecosystem.
projects.problem_statement: The University of Rwanda previously relied on manual processes for venue booking, event registration, graduation attendance, and gown management. These paper-based workflows created scheduling conflicts, long queues, limited attendance tracking, delayed reporting, and difficulties managing thousands of participants during large institutional events.
projects.solution: HitamoSpace digitizes the complete event management lifecycle through venue booking, online registration, QR-code attendance verification, graduation registration, companion and guest confirmation, gown issuance and returns, payment management, and real-time analytics dashboards.
projects.results:
Successfully managed 16,000+ graduation participants digitally.

Registered 6,000+ graduands and 10,000+ companions and guests.

Digitized gown application, payment, return, and fine management.

Implemented QR-code attendance verification and live event analytics.

Improved venue booking, event coordination, and institutional reporting.
projects.impact: HitamoSpace has transformed institutional event management by supporting both everyday university events and large-scale ceremonies. It successfully managed the University of Rwanda 11th Graduation Ceremony, serving 16,000+ users, including 6,000+ graduands and 10,000+ companions and guests, while improving coordination, reducing queues, strengthening transparency, and providing real-time decision-making statistics.
projects.future_plans:
Mobile application for event organizers.

Digital event ticketing and badges.

AI-powered attendance analytics.

Integration with Binary Pay for seamless payments.

Expansion to conferences, workshops, and external institutional events.

projects.title: INUMA App
projects.description: INUMA is the  digital request management platform developed by UR Binary Hub to streamline the submission, approval, tracking, reporting, and monitoring of institutional requests across all colleges and administrative units.
projects.full_description:
INUMA is a flagship homegrown digital solution developed by UR Binary Hub to transform how administrative requests are managed across the University of Rwanda. The platform digitizes previously paper-based workflows by providing a centralized system where students, academic staff, administrative staff, and management can submit, process, approve, monitor, and report institutional requests in real time.

Initially designed to manage local mission requests, INUMA has evolved into a comprehensive workflow management platform supporting multiple institutional processes. It provides role-based dashboards, automated approval workflows, digital document management, financial tracking, notifications, reporting tools, and analytics that significantly improve transparency, accountability, and operational efficiency.

Today, INUMA serves all University of Rwanda colleges and administrative units, processing thousands of requests while eliminating unnecessary paperwork and accelerating decision-making.
projects.problem_statement:
Before INUMA, most institutional requests at the University of Rwanda were handled through paper forms, emails, and manual approval processes. This created numerous operational challenges, including:

Slow approval processes.

Excessive paperwork.

Difficulty tracking request status.

Lost or duplicated documents.

Limited transparency for applicants.

Manual financial calculations.

Delayed reporting and monitoring.

High administrative workload across colleges and headquarters.

With thousands of requests processed annually, the University required a scalable digital solution capable of standardizing workflows while providing real-time visibility to both applicants and management.
projects.solution:
INUMA provides a centralized digital workflow platform that automates the complete lifecycle of institutional requests.

Core features include:

Digital request submission.

Multi-level approval workflows.

Role-based dashboards.

Local mission management.

Financial calculation and payment tracking.

Digital approval letters.

Mission report submission.

Query and revision management.

Document attachment management.

Automated notifications.

Real-time analytics dashboards.

Institutional reporting.

Paper-saving monitoring.

College and campus performance tracking.

The platform integrates administrative processes into a single digital ecosystem, ensuring that every stakeholder—from applicants to senior management—can perform their responsibilities efficiently.
projects.results:
6,328+ institutional requests processed digitally.

4,382 requests approved with an 82.9% report compliance rate.

99,513 papers saved through paperless workflows.

RWF 320,710,979 processed with 100% payment completion.

85.3% of requests completed within 0–2 days.

Successfully adopted across the University of Rwanda's colleges and administrative units, significantly reducing processing time and improving service delivery.
projects.impact: INUMA has transformed institutional request management across the University of Rwanda by digitizing workflows in all colleges and units. The platform has processed 6,328+ requests, achieved 4,382 approvals, saved an estimated 99,513 papers, managed RWF 320.7 million in request-related transactions, and improved transparency, accountability, and administrative efficiency.
projects.future_plans:
Future enhancements planned for INUMA include:

Integration with Binary Pay for seamless institutional payments.

Expanded workflow modules beyond mission management.

Mobile application support.

Advanced AI-powered analytics.

Digital signature integration.

Cross-system integration with StudenTrak and other UR platforms.

Enhanced reporting and executive dashboards.

Public service request modules for additional university services.

projects.title: UMUTUNGO Box
projects.description: Umutungo Box is a comprehensive digital asset management system developed to help institutions register, track, assign, transfer, maintain, depreciate, and monitor physical assets through a centralized and transparent platform.
projects.full_description:
Umutungo Box is a flagship homegrown digital solution developed by UR Binary Hub at the University of Rwanda to modernize institutional asset management. The platform replaces paper-based and spreadsheet-driven asset management processes with a secure, centralized, and intelligent digital system.

The system enables institutions to manage the complete lifecycle of physical assets—from procurement and registration to assignment, transfers, maintenance, depreciation, audits, and disposal—while providing real-time dashboards, QR-code tracking, approval workflows, and comprehensive reporting.

Designed to support multi-campus institutions such as the University of Rwanda, Umutungo Box improves accountability, transparency, compliance, and operational efficiency across colleges, schools, departments, and administrative units.
projects.problem_statement:
The University of Rwanda and many public institutions have traditionally managed physical assets using manual registers, spreadsheets, and paper documentation. This approach created numerous challenges, including:

Difficulty tracking asset ownership and locations.

Poor visibility of assigned assets.

Time-consuming asset audits.

Manual depreciation calculations.

Limited accountability for asset transfers.

Weak maintenance tracking.

Delays in reporting and decision-making.

Risk of asset loss or duplication.

These challenges highlighted the need for a centralized digital asset management platform.
projects.solution: Developed a comprehensive web-based system for asset registration, tracking, and depreciation calculation.
projects.results:
The project has achieved several important milestones:

Completed full system development.

Successful demonstrations to University management.

Positive validation from SPIU leadership.

Identified as a strategic institutional solution.

Workshop implementation roadmap prepared.

Ready for institution-wide deployment after capacity-building and rollout activities.
projects.impact:
Umutungo Box delivers significant institutional benefits:

Eliminates manual asset registers.

Improves accountability through digital ownership records.

Enables faster asset audits.

Strengthens transparency across campuses.

Reduces asset losses.

Supports data-driven planning.

Automates depreciation calculations.

Improves maintenance management.

Enhances compliance with institutional asset policies.

The system has attracted interest from the University of Rwanda's SPIU (Single Project Implementation Unit) as a strategic solution for managing university assets across all campuses.
projects.future_plans:
Future enhancements include:

Integration with procurement workflows.

Supplier management.

Delivery note management.

Receiving committee workflows.

Security gate asset movement tracking.

Integration with StockBox for consumable inventory.

Mobile QR-code scanning application.

Multi-institution deployment beyond the University of Rwanda.

projects.title: StudenTrak
projects.description: StudenTrak is an integrated student lifecycle management system developed under UR Binary Hub to digitize applications, admissions, registration, finance, academic records, and student services across higher learning institutions.
projects.full_description:
StudenTrak is a flagship homegrown digital solution developed under UR Binary Hub at the University of Rwanda to modernize student management from admission to graduation. The platform centralizes undergraduate and postgraduate applications, admissions, registration, finance, academic records, and student services into a single digital ecosystem.

Designed as a scalable higher education management platform, StudenTrak provides role-based dashboards for applicants, students, registrars, finance officers, academic staff, and university management, streamlining institutional processes while improving transparency, efficiency, and student experience.
projects.problem_statement: Many universities rely on fragmented systems and manual processes for student admissions, registration, finance, and academic management. This creates delays, duplicate records, heavy paperwork, limited tracking, and inefficient coordination between academic and administrative offices.
projects.solution: StudenTrak digitizes the entire student lifecycle through online applications, admission management, student registration, finance integration, academic record management, role-based dashboards, automated notifications, and real-time reporting in a centralized platform.
projects.results:
Digitized undergraduate and postgraduate admission workflows.

Centralized student registration and academic records.

Integrated finance and administrative processes.

Automated notifications and approval workflows.

Improved reporting and decision-making across university offices.
projects.impact: StudenTrak simplifies university operations by improving admission efficiency, strengthening student record management, reducing paperwork, enhancing transparency, and providing management with real-time academic and administrative insights.
projects.future_plans:
Integration with Binary Pay for online payments.

Mobile application for students and staff.

AI-powered admission analytics.

Graduation and alumni management.

Expansion to other higher learning institutions.

blog_posts.excerpt: UR Binary Hub supported prospective students during the 2026 University of Rwanda application period, providing guidance and technical assistance throughout the application process. The initiative helped applicants better understand the application requirements and navigate the online application process with confidence.
blog_posts.content:
UR Application 2026 Support by UR Binary Hub

From 20 September to 5 October 2026, UR Binary Hub supported prospective students during the University of Rwanda 2026 application period.

The initiative provided applicants with guidance on application requirements, programme selection, online application procedures, and technical challenges. Through this support, the Hub helped students navigate the application process with greater confidence.

The initiative reflects UR Binary Hub’s commitment to using technology and innovation to improve access to education and support the University of Rwanda community. It also provided Hub members with an opportunity to engage with applicants, understand their challenges, and provide practical solutions.

Through initiatives like this, UR Binary Hub continues to connect technology, innovation, education, and community impact while empowering the next generation of students.

UR Binary Hub — The Power of United Minds.

blog_posts.content:

The University of Rwanda Binary Hub (TEKiNOVA Hub) continues to transform ideas into practical digital solutions through innovation, collaboration, and mentorship.

From 25–29 October 2026, NDAYISHIMIYE Habibu, a Computer Science graduate and Hub volunteer innovator, represents the University of Rwanda at the 5th Afretec Annual Conference in Johannesburg, South Africa, under the theme “Transcending Boundaries: Engineering Africa’s Inclusive Digital Future.”

The conference provides an opportunity to exchange knowledge, explore emerging technologies, and strengthen collaboration among African universities and innovation communities.

Through projects such as INUMA and Umutungo Box, the Hub demonstrates how collaborative software development can improve institutional processes and build technical capacity.

Guided by its motto, “The Power of United Minds,” UR Binary Hub remains committed to advancing inclusive digital transformation and turning innovation into meaningful impact.

From ideas to innovation, and from innovation to impact.
